Two ORCA NMR jobs from `files/`. `NMR_ORCA.out` has ¹H shieldings and H–H couplings
(`%eprnmr nuclei = all H {shift, SSALL}`) for C18H16O4S. `nmr.out` has ¹H, ¹³C, ¹⁵N and ¹⁰⁷Ag shieldings for
a 204-atom Ag₄ complex. Both use the built-in default references, as no TMS output is available.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/NMR_ORCA.out` — ORCA, B3LYP D4 def2-TZVPP CPCM(CHCl3) NMR, J(H,H), C18H16O4S
* `files/nmr.out` — ORCA, B3LYP D4 def2-TZVPP CPCM(CHCl3) NMR, H/C/N/Ag shieldings and couplings, C60H84Ag4N24O32

**1. Proton shifts, couplings and NOE.** Only the first part of the output is shown.

```bash
frog-nmr files/NMR_ORCA.out -n H
```

* With `-n H` only the 16 protons are listed (Index 23–38, labels H24–H39). Since no `--ref` is given,
  the default 1H reference is used: δ = 31.8 − σ for these values (e.g. H26: σ 23.443 → δ 8.357 ppm).
* The output has 16 H atoms, more than the 15-atom limit for matrices, so J is printed as a pair list.
  Geminal couplings are negative: H30/H31 −11.995 Hz (a CH₂), and H37–H39 about −9 Hz, inside the
  methyl group, which is not visible in the spectrum. The ortho couplings of the aromatic rings are
  6.426–6.916 Hz.
* The NOE table that follows (cut here) lists the H···H pairs within 5 Å (`--r-cutoff`)
  with their relative NOE.

**2. Simulated ¹H and COSY spectra at 400 MHz.**

```bash
frog-nmr files/NMR_ORCA.out --sim-1d --cosy --freq 400 --plot --dpi 150
```

```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-nmr/NMR_ORCA_1d_1h.png
Simulated ¹H spectrum (400 MHz, full spin simulation, methyl H merged).
```

```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-nmr/NMR_ORCA_cosy_1h_1h.png
:width: 70%
:alt: Simulated ¹H–¹H COSY.

Simulated ¹H–¹H COSY.
```

The three methyl protons H37–H39 are merged into one 3H signal at 4.248 ppm (the mean σ, 27.552 ppm).
This gives the tallest line of the 1D spectrum. All the other protons are single signals: the molecule
has no other symmetry. The multiplets come from the exact spin simulation with the computed J, and the
ppm axis decreases to the right. In the COSY, the cross peaks connect the coupled aromatic protons
(6.7–8.4 ppm) and the signals near 3.9–4.2 ppm.

**3. Edited ¹H–¹³C HSQC of the large complex.** The signal tables are long, so only the end of the
output is shown.

```bash
frog-nmr files/nmr.out -n 1H 13C --hsqc --freq 400 --plot --dpi 150
```

```text
…
│ C173      │ 1 │     155.253 │       29.753 │ C173             │

ℹ  Computing 2D 1H-13C HSQC / direct correlation spectrum...
✔  Saved plot: files/nmr_hsqc_1h_13c.png
```

```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-nmr/nmr_hsqc_1h_13c.png
:width: 70%
:alt: Simulated multiplicity-edited HSQC (CH/CH₃ positive, CH₂ negative).

Simulated multiplicity-edited HSQC (CH/CH₃ positive, CH₂ negative).
```

Each CH pair with |J| > 40 Hz or r < 1.45 Å gives a cross peak. CH₂ groups (red, negative) appear
around δ(¹³C) 75 ppm and δ(¹H) 3–5 ppm; CH and CH₃ are blue. The axes use the default references (no
TMS output was available for this method). For a real comparison, pass `--ref tms.out` computed at the
same level.
